new.title: Climb to the Pontic king tombs above Amasya
new.desc: Rock-cut tombs of the Pontic kings, carved into the limestone cliff above the Yeşilırmak in the 4th-3rd centuries BC when Amasya (Amaseia) was the Pontic capital. Only a few of the original tombs survive; they are on the UNESCO Tentative List with Harşena mountain.
new.tip: Go late afternoon for light on the cliff; a terrace cafe by the ticket office looks over the town.
new.q: Kral Kaya Mezarları, Harşena Mahallesi, Amasya Merkez, Amasya

new.title: Hike up Harşena Castle for the Amasya skyline
new.desc: Fortress on Mt Harşena with Hellenistic, Roman, Byzantine and Ottoman layers, once defended by eight rings of walls and a tunnel of about 150 steps cut down through the rock. From the top the Yeşilırmak gorge and the whole town are laid out below.
new.tip: Allow 45 minutes on foot and carry water; opening hours vary by season, so check at the gate.
new.q: Harşena Kalesi (Amasya Kalesi), Harşena Mahallesi, Amasya Merkez, Amasya

new.title: Stroll the Yalıboyu houses along the Yeşilırmak
new.desc: Row of half-timbered Ottoman waterfront houses on the north bank of the Yeşilırmak, many restored as hotels, cafes and restaurants. Set against the lit cliffs and tombs, it is the classic Amasya view.
new.tip: Best at dusk when the tombs are floodlit; cross one of the old bridges for the reflection photo.
new.q: Yalıboyu Evleri, Büyük Ağa Caddesi, Bahçeleriçi Mahallesi, Amasya Merkez, Amasya

new.title: Step inside the Hazeranlar Mansion
new.desc: Two-storey timber Ottoman mansion built in 1865 for the Hazeran family on the south bank, restored as a museum house. It shows the layout of a well-off Amasya home, with carved ceilings and separate men's and women's quarters.
new.tip: Ground-floor rooms are furnished; ask for a guided walk-through if offered.
new.q: Hazeranlar Konağı, Hatuniye Mahallesi, Amasya Merkez, Amasya

new.title: See the Ilkhanid mummies at Amasya Museum
new.desc: Archaeological museum with Hittite, Pontic, Roman and Ottoman finds and a famed hall of 14th-century Ilkhanid mummies. A Hittite bronze figure and Roman jewellery are among the other highlights.
new.tip: Allow about an hour; the mummy room is at the back of the main gallery.
new.q: Amasya Müzesi, Atatürk Caddesi, Amasya Merkez, Amasya

new.title: Visit the Sultan Bayezid II Complex
new.desc: Külliye completed in 1486 by Sultan Bayezid II, who had been governor of Amasya as a prince. The mosque, with its large domed prayer hall, sits in a quiet courtyard with a medrese and imaret.
new.tip: Visit outside prayer times; the courtyard shade is pleasant in summer.
new.q: Sultan II. Bayezid Külliyesi, Beyazıt Paşa Mahallesi, Amasya Merkez, Amasya

new.title: Admire the Gök Medrese mosque's blue tilework
new.desc: Gök Medrese Camii, built in 1266-67 by the Seljuk emir Torumtay, has a dark stone portal and blue-glazed tile. It was a medrese that later became a mosque, still in use today.
new.tip: Look at the carved stone portal first; entry is free outside prayer times.
new.q: Gökmedrese Camii, Ferhat Sokak, Gökmedrese Mahallesi, Amasya Merkez, Amasya

new.title: Hear the music therapy at the Amasya Bimarhane
new.desc: Ilkhanid hospital founded in 1308 where mental illness was treated with music, water sounds and scents. The domed hall with its central pool served as a sound-therapy ward; Amasya-born surgeon Sabuncuoğlu is remembered here.
new.tip: Staged music-therapy displays run in the main hall; allow 30 minutes.
new.q: Amasya Bimarhanesi (Darüşşifa), Mehmet Paşa Mahallesi, Amasya Merkez, Amasya

new.title: Walk the Kapıağa Medresesi courtyard
new.desc: Ottoman medrese built in 1488 by Hüseyin Ağa, chief white eunuch of Bayezid II. Its arcaded courtyard is one of the quietest corners of the old town.
new.tip: Pause in the shaded yard; opening times vary.
new.q: Büyük Ağa Medresesi (Kapıağa Medresesi), Medrese Sokak, Amasya Merkez, Amasya

new.title: Buy Amasya çöreği at Galip Amasya Çörekçisi
new.desc: Amasya çöreği is a yeast pastry with a nut and seed filling that keeps for days, so it is the local edible souvenir. Galip is a named bakery serving it fresh.
new.tip: Go in the morning and buy a packaged box to take home; pair with tea.
new.q: Galip Amasya Çörekçisi, Habibi Sokak, Pirinççi Mahallesi, Amasya Merkez, Amasya

new.title: Order bakla dolması at Amaseia Mutfağı
new.desc: Amaseia Mutfağı is repeatedly named for Amasya home cooking: bakla dolması (broad-bean dolma) and the aubergine dish patlıcan çullaması.
new.tip: Ask what is seasonal; bakla dolması is a spring dish.
new.q: Amaseia Mutfağı, Amasya Merkez, Amasya

new.title: See the Kara Mustafa Paşa Külliyesi in Merzifon
new.desc: Ottoman complex of the 17th-century grand vizier Kara Mustafa Paşa: mosque (c. 1666), bedesten, Taşhan caravanserai, hamam and medrese. The Taşhan is a two-storey han with shops around a courtyard.
new.tip: Start at the mosque, then walk through the Taşhan and bedesten next door.
new.q: Kara Mustafa Paşa Külliyesi, Gazimahbup Mahallesi, Merzifon, Amasya

new.title: Eat topuz kebabı at Bedesten Osmanlı Mutfağı
new.desc: Restaurant inside the 17th-century Kara Mustafa Paşa complex serving Ottoman dishes; its chef highlights topuz kebabı, a slow-cooked lamb dish of the Amasya area.
new.tip: Open until late; sit in the courtyard in summer.
new.q: Bedesten Osmanlı Mutfağı, Taşhan Sokak, Gazimahbup Mahallesi, Merzifon, Amasya

new.title: Walk around Lake Borabay in the mountains
new.desc: Mountain lake at about 1,050 m by Borabay village in Taşova district, a quiet spot with rest areas and trout farming, about 17 km from Taşova.
new.tip: Take a picnic and walk the shoreline; it is coolest in summer.
new.q: Borabay Gölü, Borabay, Taşova, Amasya

new.title: Tour Latifoğlu Mansion in Tokat
new.desc: Ottoman Baroque konak on Gazi Osman Paşa Boulevard, now a museum house with carved wood, plaster and pencil-work decoration. Its date is disputed between 1746 and 1874 depending on source.
new.tip: Allow 45 minutes; opening days vary.
new.q: Latifoğlu Konağı, Gazi Osman Paşa Bulvarı No:207, Camikebir Mahallesi, Tokat Merkez, Tokat

new.title: Visit Tokat Museum in the Arastalı Bedesten
new.desc: The Tokat Museum has occupied the old Arastalı Bedesten since 2012 and shows archaeology, ethnography and fine yazma (hand-printed cloth) examples under the bedesten domes.
new.tip: Plan one hour; the bedesten building is itself the main exhibit.
new.q: Tokat Müzesi, Arastalı Bedesten, Tokat Merkez, Tokat

new.title: Soak in the Ali Paşa Hamamı
new.desc: Part of the 1572 Ali Paşa complex, this Ottoman hamam still operates with separate sections for men and women, next to the Ali Paşa mosque at the foot of Sulusokak.
new.tip: Take a towel and arrive early; men and women have separate hours.
new.q: Ali Paşa Hamamı, Sulusokak, Tokat Merkez, Tokat

new.title: Watch hand-block yazma printing at Yazmacılar Hanı
new.desc: Yazmacılar Hanı (Gazioğlu Hanı) is named for Tokat's hand-block printing of cloth, practised for centuries with wood blocks and natural dyes. Workshops show the stamping and sell scarves and tablecloths.
new.tip: Ask a master to demonstrate printing; buy directly from the printers.
new.q: Yazmacılar Hanı, Halit Sokak No:3, Kabe-i Mescit Mahallesi, Tokat Merkez, Tokat

new.title: Climb Tokat Castle for the view over the town
new.desc: Ruined castle on a rocky hill above the old town, with Byzantine and Seljuk-era walls. From the top, the Yeşilırmak plain and Tokat's domes are visible.
new.tip: Go in the morning or at sunset; wear sturdy shoes.
new.q: Tokat Kalesi, Tokat Merkez, Tokat

new.title: Explore Ballıca Cave near Pazar
new.desc: Fossil cave in Permian-Triassic marble about 6 km southeast of Pazar, around 68 m long, with stalactite and stalagmite halls, a Fossil Hall and dwarf-bat colonies. The air is oxygen-rich and the cave is lit for visitors.
new.tip: Bring a light jacket; a weekend breakfast spot, Değirmendere, sits nearby.
new.q: Ballıca Mağarası, Pazar, Tokat

new.title: Walk the walls of Niksar Castle
new.desc: Danishmend-era fortress said to be second in size only to Diyarbakır's walls in Türkiye. Niksar was the Danishmend capital and has many surviving Seljuk and Danishmend monuments.
new.tip: Combine with the Ulu Cami and the Kırkkızlar tomb.
new.q: Niksar Kalesi, Niksar, Tokat

new.title: See the 12th-century Niksar Ulu Cami
new.desc: Niksar Ulu Cami is dated to 1145 though without an inscription, and attributed to Çepnizâde Hasan Bey. Mehmed the Conqueror is said to have spent Ramadan here on his Trabzon campaign.
new.tip: Visit outside prayer times.
new.q: Niksar Ulu Cami, Niksar, Tokat

new.title: Climb Zile Castle and its Roman rock theatre
new.desc: Zile Castle stands on a mound with a Roman-era acropolis and a small Roman theatre carved into the rock on its north-east flank. Zile is ancient Zela, of Caesar's veni, vidi, vici.
new.tip: Climb at the cooler end of the day; walk the old town below.
new.q: Zile Kalesi, Zile, Tokat

new.title: Wander the ruins of Sebastopolis at Sulusaray
new.desc: Sebastopolis, an ancient Roman city at Sulusaray, with an open-air museum of columns and city remains.
new.tip: Check access before going; it is off the main road.
new.q: Sebastopolis Antik Kenti, Sulusaray, Tokat

new.title: Eat Tokat kebabı at Pirhan
new.desc: Pirhan, opposite the Meydan Camii, serves Tokat kebabı (lamb, aubergine and potato baked together) plus bakla sarması and pehli pilav by order.
new.tip: Order bakla sarması a day ahead.
new.q: Pirhan Restaurant, Meydan Caddesi No:16/A, Yarahmet Mahallesi, Tokat Merkez, Tokat

new.title: Try bat and katmer at Saklıbahçe
new.desc: Saklıbahçe on the Sivas road is known for Tokat kebabı, bat (cold green lentil and bulgur dish with herbs and walnut), katmer and çökelekli pide.
new.tip: Bat is served cold; order it as a starter.
new.q: Saklıbahçe Restaurant, Beybağı Mahallesi, Sivas Yolu, Geyras Mevkii, Tokat Merkez, Tokat

new.title: Order çökelekli pide at İşeri Restaurant
new.desc: İşeri on the Sivas road in Geyras is listed for çökelekli pide, Tokat kebabı, Osmanlı kavurması, kuzu tandır and revani.
new.tip: Order the pide first; it is a few km from the centre.
new.q: İşeri Restaurant, Sivas Caddesi No:104, Geyras, Tokat Merkez, Tokat

new.title: Eat country food by Almus Lake at Almus Şehri Sefa
new.desc: Almus Şehri Sefa is a lakeside restaurant and bungalow site near Almus, serving traditional Turkish dishes and breakfast made with produce from its garden and the lake. Tripadvisor ranks it among Tokat's top restaurants.
new.tip: Ask about the catch of the day, and come in daylight for the view over the lake.
new.q: Almus Şehri Sefa, Sırakayalar Mevkii, Almus, Tokat

new.title: Walk the Lion Gate and temples of Hattuşa
new.desc: Hattuşa, capital of the Hittite Empire near Boğazkale, a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1986. The Lion Gate, Great Temple and Yerkapı rampart are the key stops on a loop of several kilometres.
new.tip: Drive the loop; start early, there is little shade.
new.q: Hattuşa Ören Yeri, Boğazkale, Çorum

new.title: See the Hittite gods at Yazılıkaya
new.desc: Open-air Hittite rock sanctuary about 2 km north of Hattuşa, with processions of gods and goddesses carved into natural rock chambers.
new.tip: Visit together with Hattuşa.
new.q: Yazılıkaya Açık Hava Tapınağı, Boğazkale, Çorum

new.title: Visit Alacahöyük and its Early Bronze royal tombs
new.desc: Alacahöyük was among Türkiye's first national excavations (begun 1935 under R.O. Arık). The museum on site holds grave finds from 13 Early Bronze Age royal tombs.
new.tip: Visit the site museum; allow 1.5 hours.
new.q: Alacahöyük Ören Yeri ve Müzesi, Alacahöyük, Alaca, Çorum

new.title: Explore Şapinuva, a Hittite capital near Ortaköy
new.desc: Şapinuva was a major military, religious and administrative centre of the Hittite Empire, excavated since 1988. A 3,300-year-old bronze helmet from here is displayed in Çorum Museum.
new.tip: Bring water; the site is 3 km from Ortaköy.
new.q: Şapinuva Ören Yeri, Ortaköy, Çorum

new.title: See the Hittite helmet at Çorum Museum
new.desc: Çorum Museum, opened in 1968, shows archaeological and ethnographic items, including the 3,300-year-old Hittite helmet from Şapinuva.
new.tip: Visit before the Hittite sites to orient yourself.
new.q: Çorum Müzesi, Çorum Merkez, Çorum

new.title: Meet the Çorum Clock Tower
new.desc: Çorum's clock tower, built in 1894, is the city's central landmark and stands next to Veli Paşa Hanı.
new.tip: Stop here before the han and leblebi shops.
new.q: Çorum Saat Kulesi, Çorum Merkez, Çorum

new.title: Browse Veli Paşa Hanı
new.desc: 19th-century han near the clock tower, with the Çorum City Museum upstairs and a regional-food cafe on the ground floor.
new.tip: Combine with the leblebi shops.
new.q: Veli Paşa Hanı, Çorum Merkez, Çorum

new.title: See Çorum Ulu Cami
new.desc: Çorum Ulu Cami, in the old market area, dates from Seljuk times though much rebuilt.
new.tip: Visit outside prayer times.
new.q: Çorum Ulu Cami, Çorum Merkez, Çorum

new.title: See the Roman rock tombs of İskilip
new.desc: Rock tombs thought to be Roman, on the south slope of İskilip Castle.
new.tip: Climb the castle hill after lunch.
new.q: İskilip Kaya Mezarları, İskilip, Çorum

new.title: Cross the Koyunbaba Bridge at Osmancık
new.desc: Koyunbaba Bridge over the Kızılırmak at Osmancık, built in the reign of Bayezid II.
new.tip: Stroll along the river afterwards.
new.q: Koyunbaba Köprüsü, Osmancık, Çorum

new.title: Find the Kapılıkaya rock tomb at Laçin
new.desc: Kapılıkaya is a rock tomb near Laçin, listed among Çorum's historical sites.
new.tip: Check access before the trip.
new.q: Kapılıkaya Kaya Mezarı, Laçin, Çorum

new.title: Buy fresh-roasted leblebi at Leblebi Ocağı in Osmancık
new.desc: Leblebi Ocağı is a roasted chickpea shop at the Osmancık exit of the Samsun-Istanbul road. It roasts leblebi daily and keeps it in wooden crates; leblebi is Çorum province's trademark snack.
new.tip: Buy a bag by weight and ask for the freshest batch; it has a tea area and parking.
new.q: Leblebi Ocağı, Samsun-İstanbul Yolu Osmancık Çıkışı, Osmancık, Çorum

new.title: Eat tandır kebab at Erdalın Yeri
new.desc: Erdalın Yeri is a Çorum city restaurant on Hıdırlık Sokak serving tandır kebab over rice, with pide and salad ordered separately. Tea is served free after the meal.
new.tip: Order the pide and salad on the side; they are not included with the kebab.
new.q: Erdalın Yeri, Hıdırlık Sokak No:4, Çepni Mahallesi, Çorum Merkez, Çorum
